Her career includes service as a judge on the International Criminal Court, the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda, and the High Court of South Africa, as well as serving as the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights. entry.title: Victorian Elites and the Role of Soft Skills in Their Success
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | worksinprogress.co | hacker news

Nineteenth-century British elites achieved significant global dominance by prioritizing social networking and character formation over STEM-focused education and technical rigor. While modern success models often emphasize extreme discipline and scientific expertise, the Victorian ruling class used boarding schools and Oxbridge to foster leadership, "gentlemanly conduct," and intense interpersonal loyalty.

This educational and social structure created a highly interconnected and cooperative ruling class through organized sports and student self-governance. Such an emphasis on social capital, rather than individual technical competence, may have provided the stability and collective efficacy required to manage a global empire and industrial dominance.

entry.title: ADHD Linked to Delayed Circadian Rhythms and Melatonin Onset
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | frontiersin.org | hacker news

Research indicates that a significant subgroup of individuals with ADHD exhibits circadian rhythm dysfunction, characterized by evening chronotype and delayed biological markers such as melatonin and cortisol. Studies show that up to 80% of adults and 82% of children with ADHD experience sleep disturbances, with dim-light melatonin onset typically delayed by 45 to 90 minutes.

Behavioral circadian interventions—such as bright light therapy, melatonin supplementation, and structured sleep hygiene—are proposed as adjunct treatments for ADHD to improve core symptoms. Evidence suggests that advancing the circadian phase can mitigate symptoms, supporting a clinical model that includes routine screening for sleep and circadian disturbances.

China currently serves as the global cost benchmark for storage through domestic supply chain integration. In the Middle East and Africa, storage costs are projected to decrease 33% to $80/MWh by 2035, further accelerating the displacement of gas-peaking power.

entry.title: Researchers Sequence Genome of Jonathan, the World's Oldest Living Land Animal
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | 404media.co | source | hacker news

Researchers have sequenced the genome and methylome of Jonathan, an Aldabra giant tortoise estimated to be 194 years old and the world's oldest living land animal. The study, published in Science Advances, identified unique gene variants in aging pathways, including DNA repair, insulin regulation, and mitochondrial function.

Analysis revealed that Jonathan's mitochondrial methylome exhibits "low entropy," appearing similar to that of a five-year-old tortoise despite his extreme age. Researchers from the Kallel Foundation aim to use these epigenetic insights to help identify potential biological targets for extending human healthspan and lifespan.

entry.title: Vladimir Reshetnikov Identified as Mathematical Pseudonym Cleo

The "Cleo" pseudonym on Math Stack Exchange, famous for providing precise, closed-form solutions to complex integration problems without showing any work, has been identified as Vladimir Reshetnikov. During an active period between 2013 and 2015, the account provided correct answers to difficult mathematical questions, sparking debates over whether the poster was a single genius or a collective of scholars.

Investigators eventually linked Reshetnikov to the persona through digital evidence, including email recovery information. Reshetnikov explained that the pseudonym and its terse, unproven answers were intended to stimulate interest in challenging mathematical problems and to encourage users to develop their own problem-solving methodologies.

entry.title: OpenAI Withdraws Three Math Papers Over Sign Error
entry.content:

OpenAI has withdrawn three mathematics manuscripts following the discovery of a sign error in a paper titled “Algebraicity of Weil classes on split abelian eightfolds.” The error invalidates a stabilization-trace cancellation argument and affects two dependent papers: “Algebraicity of Kuga–Satake Correspondences for K3 Surfaces” and “The rational Hodge conjecture for products of K3 surfaces.”

In addition to the withdrawals, OpenAI has revised 14 other manuscripts to correct proof arguments and clarify hypotheses. The update also includes six new formalizations, bringing the total percentage of formalized top-line results to approximately 42% of the 719 total results recorded in the project.

entry.title: AI Autoformalization of Navier-Stokes Proof Lacks Semantic Fidelity in Lean Verification
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | arxiv.org | hacker news

Verification of AI-translated formal proofs in the Lean language does not guarantee the correctness of the original natural language mathematical arguments. Using OpenAI's Navier-Stokes solutions as a case study, researchers demonstrate that the formal Lean code often fails to correspond semantically to the accompanying natural language proofs.

The study highlights that resolving linguistic ambiguities in mathematical text is a task of infinite Solvability Complexity Index (SCI), making semantically faithful autoformalization more difficult than the Halting problem. This finding suggests that mechanical verification of formal code cannot currently serve as a reliable safeguard for the integrity of natural language mathematical reasoning.

Discoveries in non-linear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric organic synthesis have earned Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai the 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry. Their research explains the spontaneous emergence of homochirality, the phenomenon in which chemical reactions favor one mirror-image molecular form over another.

This work resolves a century-old mystery regarding how life's molecular asymmetry originated. Such control over molecular handedness is vital for pharmaceutical manufacturing, where the specific orientation of a molecule determines its biological efficacy.

entry.title: Global Analysis Finds Ecosystem Resilience to Species Loss Is Overestimated
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | phys.org | source | hacker news

Ecosystem resilience to species loss is significantly lower than previously assumed, according to a global study in *Nature Ecology & Evolution*. Analyzing 222,829 data points across land, freshwater, and marine environments, the study found that ecosystem services—such as water purification and carbon storage—decline steadily as biodiversity decreases, rather than leveling off after a certain number of species are present.

Ocean carbon sequestration shows the strongest positive response to biodiversity, suggesting that "blue carbon" sinks depend on diverse marine communities, though researchers note this specific finding requires further study. While services like coastal flood protection may rely on specific foundational species rather than overall diversity, other benefits such as natural pest control are heavily dependent on high biodiversity levels.

entry.title: AI Agents Identify Two Room-Temperature Magnetic Semiconductor Candidates
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | vals.ai | hacker news

Research using AI agents has identified two potential Luttinger-compensated (LC) semiconductor candidates for next-generation spintronic memory. These materials are predicted to maintain zero net magnetism while allowing for spin sorting across significant energy windows at room temperature. The candidates include a newly designed compound, YBaMnFeO₅, and an existing material from 1999, KV[Cr(CN)₆].

Luttinger-compensated magnets combine the benefits of ferromagnets and antiferromagnets, offering high-speed switching and high packing density without the interference of macroscopic magnetic fields. While YBaMnFeO₅ may face synthesis challenges due to its required atomic arrangement, KV[Cr(CN)₆] shows significant promise because it has already been synthesized and exhibits magnetic stability above room temperature.

Nolla Health is launching a pilot program in Utah that uses artificial intelligence to diagnose skin conditions and issue prescriptions for acne medications without direct human oversight. This initiative represents a first in the United States, as it operates under a state regulatory agreement that allows AI technology to perform medical roles traditionally reserved for physicians.

The service is delivered via the Nolla Derm app, which uses facial scans and digital intake forms to generate automated treatment recommendations. The pilot is available to Utah residents aged 18 and older and aims to streamline access to dermatological care by reducing the need for traditional clinical consultations.

entry.title: Ukraine Deploys Distributed Renewables to Increase Energy Resilience Against Infrastructure Attacks
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | energytransition.org | hacker news

Ukraine is rapidly adopting distributed renewable energy technologies, such as small-scale solar arrays and battery storage, to mitigate the impact of Russian strikes on the country's centralized power grid. In frontline regions like Mykolaiv, solar-powered systems are being used to maintain essential services, including desalination and water pumping, ensuring that residential areas retain access to drinking water even when the main electrical infrastructure is offline.

This security-driven transition shifts the focus from large, vulnerable thermal and hydro plants toward decentralized, flexible generation assets that are harder to target and quicker to repair. While the rapid rollout of solar and storage is being driven by immediate survival needs, it also aligns with Ukraine's long-term goals to modernize its energy sector and meet European Union climate standards.
